macros.name: alert
macros.doc: The \alert{. . . } command is compatible with the beamer class. It puts highlighted text in boldface.

macros.name: featuresize
macros.doc: Use the \featuresize{⟨size⟩} command to adjust the size of features in \feat{. . . }.

macros.name: fleft
macros.doc: The \fleft (function left) declaration gives the left bracket.

macros.name: fmat
macros.doc: The \fmat{. . . }{. . . }command is for feature matrices. Use \fmleft and \fmright for each bracket, and for each line in the feature matrix, use \fmat{w}ith its two arguments.

macros.name: form
macros.doc: You can use the \form{. . . } command to put anything into math mode.

macros.name: fright
macros.doc: The \fright (function right) declaration gives the right bracket.

macros.name: func
macros.doc: The \func{domain}{range} command is used for each line of the function.

macros.name: funcnot
macros.doc: Use the command \funcnot{. . . }{. . . }{. . . }{. . . }{. . . }, which allows quick writing of functions in an explicit functional notation (hence the name).

macros.name: m
macros.doc: The \m{. . . } command sets grammatical morphemes (m) in small caps.

macros.name: ol
macros.doc: The \ol{. . . } command is for object language text. It is currently set to italics, but you can change that globally or locally with a \renewcommand command.

macros.name: readas
macros.doc: Along with formal expressions, the \readas{. . . } command is used with denotations to write formal expressions out in metalanguage.

macros.name: scopebox
macros.doc: The \scopebox{. . . } command places brackets ([ ]) around an expression to signal its scope.

macros.name: set
macros.doc: The \set{. . . } and \varset{. . . } commands are used to write sets.

macros.name: type
macros.doc: The \type{. . . } command is used for writing semantic types. It places its argument in ordered pair brackets, in math mode.

macros.name: uptype
macros.doc: If you really want semantic types with upright letters, use the \uptype{. . . } command wherever you’d use \type{. . . }.

macros.name: varset
macros.doc: The \varset command (‘variable set’) writes an abstracted set.

macros.name: xbar
macros.doc: The \xbar{. . . } command places a bar over the entire head name.
